newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Bond yields spiked higher on Tuesday, weakening by 16 basis points, as investors lightened their exposure amid uncertainty surrounding possible capital outlows on July 1 when foreign exchange controls will be eased.
The rand also kicked higher, briefly touching the 4.51 level in late trade as importer and London-based dollar demand tested the unit's vulnerable side.
At 1425 GMT government's R150 loan was at its intraday worst level of 14.80 pct from 14.64 percent late on Friday.
South Africa's financial markets were closed on Monday for the Youth Day holiday.
Debt traders said there had been continuous selling during the morning session, mainly from speculators, and this had been compunded in the afternoon by weaker U.S. Treasury bonds.
"There's an undertone of concern about July 1 (when individuals will be allowed to invest offshore.) Uncertainty around that is leading people to hold back," according to one senior debt trader.
Others said that the weaker rand was also fuelling jitters.
"There are still a lot of bulls around...the economic fundamentals look good but they are all waiting for July 1," another noted.
Some went as far as saying that the debt market would be in a "rampant bull phase" if the forex relaxation deadline were not looming.
U.S. Treasury bonds were last trading at a 6.73 percent yield from 6.70 percent earlier in the day after U.S. May real earnings data rose 0.3 percent compared with a revised 0.8 percent fall before.
Among a slew of other U.S. economic data that was released, U.S. industrial production and capacity utilization also weighed on the market.
Local debt traders expected the market to continue nervous in the lead up to July 1 with a possible move up to the 14.85 percent level over the next two days.
They noted that there had been some offshore buying on the day but increasing forex jitters and a lack of buying would see the market weaken further until month-end.
Foreigners were net buyers of 21.18 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Friday after buying 139.27 million rands worth on Friday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative bond market volumes were at 4.8 billion rand from 37.99 billion on Thursday -- settlement day.
The rand also had a sickly day, briefly touching the important 4.51 level in late trade on importer and London-based dollar demand in the morning and afternoon respectively.
At 1430 GMT the unit was trading at 4.5090/5120 versus the dollar from 4.5010/5030 late on Friday.
Morning importer demand was balanced to some extent by exporter dollar supply and Reserve Bank activity, forex traders said, stemming a run above 4.51.
"The Reserve Bank has been around every day, adding liquidity and preventing the rand from running up quickly," one trader said.
He added that he expected the rand to breach 4.51 by the end of the week but that it would top out at 4.5200/5250 by July 1.

Against the crosses, the rand was at 25.1241/1630 against the yen from 25.3861/4252 yen on Friday, at 0.3840/3845 marks from 0.3840/3844 marks and at 7.3830/3925 against sterling from 7.3300/3394 previously.
On the money market, short-term rates were unchanged with three-month NCDs quoted at 16.05 percent offered and the 90-day BA rate also steady at between 15.45 to 15.60 percent.
The Reserve Bank quoted the daily shortage at 7.610 billion rand on Saturday from 7.168 billion rand on Friday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482-1003
